It's been a while since we last connected on how the Social Science Data Archive's
successor is doing. Here's a short update on what DSC has built since then, with an eye
toward the parts that touch the social sciences directly, and on an organizational
change now affecting how that work is coordinated.

::: {.tldr}
**In short:** Dataverse has grown from 9 datasets in 2020 to over 1,600 today. DSC's
Redivis platform, built around an unusable 10-terabyte national voter file, has since
processed 4.8 petabytes of restricted research data. DSC is being restructured, and
responsibility for coordinating this portfolio as a whole is no longer assigned to one
role. And GIS support disappeared in 2024, even though the demand for it never did.
:::

## A 65-year lineage {#sec-lineage}

::: {.timeline}
::: {.timeline-node}
[**1961**]{.year}
[Political Behavior Archive founded by Dwaine Marvick]{.event}
:::
::: {.timeline-node}
[**1962**]{.year}
[Founding member, Inter-university Consortium for Political and Social Research (ICPSR)]{.event}
:::
::: {.timeline-node}
[**1977**]{.year}
[Becomes the Social Science Data Archive under the Institute for Social Science Research]{.event}
:::
::: {.timeline-node}
[**2014–15**]{.year}
[MOU transfers the Archive to UCLA Library (Dean Duranti / UL Steel)]{.event}
:::
::: {.timeline-node}
[**2017–18**]{.year}
[Regular check-ins with Social Sciences (Dean Hunt, Jim Stigler) shape hub-and-spoke planning for the Archive's next chapter]{.event}
:::
::: {.timeline-node}
[**2018**]{.year}
[Data Science Center founded as the Archive's institutional home]{.event}
:::
::: {.timeline-node}
[**2026**]{.year}
[This update]{.event}
:::
:::

These check-ins were a regular practice in the Archive's early years at the Library.
This update is an attempt to pick that back up. One person bridges nearly the whole
modern era: **Jamie Jamison**, who transferred with the Archive in 2014, is still on
the DSC team today.

## DSC today, by the numbers {#sec-numbers}

{{< include _partials/kpi-headline.qmd >}}

Together, these describe a shift: DSC has grown from a specialized archive service
into general-purpose research infrastructure used across the university, not just
Social Sciences, the kind of reach the 2014 transfer was meant to enable.

## Social sciences remain a core constituency {#sec-ss-constituency}

{{< include _partials/social-science-constituency.qmd >}}

The Archive's original subscriptions from the 2014 transfer, including ICPSR
(~$47K/year) and the Roper Center (~$8K/year), moved years ago onto the Library's
general membership fund. That's what freed the Archive's original gift fund (FAU
605000-DA-56972), the same fund that came over with the transfer, to cover the AWS
infrastructure costs for Dataverse and Potree instead.

The programs above will continue in some form. What's changing is who's positioned to
keep them working together as one portfolio rather than a set of separate services.
I'd welcome the chance to walk through any of this in person. The full public
dashboard, with current figures and methodology, is at
[ucla-data-science-center.github.io/dsc-stats-reports]({{< var links.full_site >}}).
